hints: Focus on what makes structural isomers different, the way the carbon skeleton is branched, not just how the formula is written.
Count the longest chain in each formula. For $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}$ you should find one with 5 carbons in a row, one with 4 in a row, and one with 3 in a row.
Check if any two structures are just the same molecule flipped end to end or rotated, those do not count as different isomers.
walkthrough:
**Recall the three skeletons for pentane**

Think of building with 5 carbons. You can have no branches, one branch, or two branches.

$$\text{n-pentane (5-chain) , 2-methylbutane (4+1) , 2,2-dimethylpropane (3+1+1)}$$

**Check option A**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is a straight 5-chain.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is a 4-chain with one methyl branch. $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_4$ is a central C with four methyls, a 3-chain with two branches. All three are different.

**Spot the duplicates in the others**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ are the same molecule numbered from opposite ends. The skeletal options also repeat 2-methylbutane twice, just drawn rotated.

**Conclude the correct set**

Only the set with one straight chain, one singly branched chain, and one doubly branched chain gives three distinct structural isomers.

options.A: Correct. The three formulae are n-pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane. They have longest chains of 5, 4 and 3 carbons respectively, so all three carbon skeletons are different.
options.B: False. The second and third formulae look different but are identical. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ numbered from the left is the same as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ numbered from the right, both are 2-methylbutane.
options.C: False. The first skeleton is n-pentane, but the second and third skeletons are both 2-methylbutane drawn in different orientations. There is no 2,2-dimethylpropane present, so only two distinct isomers are shown.
options.D: False. The third skeleton is 2,2-dimethylpropane, but the first and second skeletons are both 2-methylbutane drawn in different orientations. The straight chain n-pentane isomer is missing, so only two distinct isomers are shown.
